passages.text: Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven with the key to the Abyss, holding in his hand a great chain.
passages.sermon:
John saw an angel.
The angel came down from heaven.
The angel had the key to the Abyss.
The angel held a great chain in his hand.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔχοντα τὴν κλεῖν τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ ἅλυσιν μεγάλην ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years.
passages.sermon:
An angel came down from heaven.
The angel had the key to the Abyss.
The angel held a great chain in his hand.
The angel seized the dragon.
The dragon is the ancient serpent.
The dragon is the devil.
The dragon is Satan.
The angel bound the dragon for a thousand years.
passages.original: καὶ ἐκράτησεν τὸν δράκοντα ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος ὅς ἐστιν Διάβολος καὶ Ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν χίλια ἔτη

passages.text: And he threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him, so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete. After that, he must be released for a brief period of time.
passages.sermon:
An angel came down from heaven.
The angel held the key to the Abyss.
The angel also held a great chain in his hand.
The angel seized the dragon.
The dragon is the ancient serpent.
The dragon is the devil and Satan.
The angel threw Satan into the Abyss.
The angel shut the Abyss.
The angel sealed the Abyss over Satan.
Satan could not deceive the nations anymore.
This lasted until the thousand years were finished.
After the thousand years, Satan must be released for a short time.
passages.original: καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον καὶ ἔκλεισεν καὶ ἐσφράγισεν ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ ἵνα μὴ πλανήσῃ ἔτι τὰ ἔθνη ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη μετὰ ταῦτα δεῖ λυθῆναι αὐτὸν μικρὸν χρόνον

passages.text: Then I saw the thrones, and those seated on them had been given authority to judge. And I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, and had not received its mark on their foreheads or hands. And they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
passages.sermon:
I saw thrones.
People sat on these thrones.
God gave these people authority to judge.
I saw the souls of people who had been beheaded.
They died because they testified about Jesus.
They died because they spoke the word of God.
I also saw people who did not worship the beast.
They did not worship the image of the beast.
They did not receive the mark of the beast on their foreheads.
They did not receive the mark of the beast on their hands.
These people came to life.
They reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνους καὶ ἐκάθισαν ἐπ’ αὐτούς καὶ κρίμα ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν πεπελεκισμένων διὰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἵτινες οὐ προσεκύνησαν τὸ θηρίον οὐδὲ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἔλαβον τὸ χάραγμα ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτῶν καὶ ἔζησαν καὶ ἐβασίλευσαν μετὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ χίλια ἔτη

passages.text: The rest of the dead did not come back to life until the thousand years were complete. This is the first resurrection.
passages.sermon: The rest of the dead did not come back to life.\r\nThey remained dead until the thousand years were complete.\r\nThe first resurrection happened before the thousand years ended.
passages.original: Οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔζησαν ἄχρι τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη αὕτη ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη

passages.text: Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with Him for a thousand years.
passages.sermon:
Those who take part in the first resurrection are blessed.
Those who take part in the first resurrection are holy.
The second death cannot harm them.
They will serve as priests of God.
They will serve as priests of Christ.
They will reign with Christ for a thousand years.
passages.original: μακάριος καὶ ἅγιος ὁ ἔχων μέρος ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπὶ τούτων ὁ δεύτερος θάνατος οὐκ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν ἀλλ’ ἔσονται ἱερεῖς τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ τὰ χίλια ἔτη

passages.text: When the thousand years are complete, Satan will be released from his prison, and will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth—Gog and Magog—to assemble them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the seashore.
passages.sermon:
Satan is a deceiver and the enemy of God.
After the thousand years are complete, Satan will be released from his prison.
Satan will go out to deceive the nations.
These nations are in the four corners of the earth.
These nations include Gog and Magog.
Satan will gather these nations for battle.
The number of these people will be very great.
Their number will be like the sand of the seashore.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν τελεσθῇ τὰ χίλια ἔτη λυθήσεται ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξελεύσεται πλανῆσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὰ ἐν ταῖς τέσσαρσιν γωνίαις τῆς γῆς τὸν Γὼγ καὶ Μαγώγ συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον ὧν ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης

passages.text: And they marched across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. But fire came down from heaven and consumed them.
passages.sermon:
A great army marched across the earth.
They surrounded the camp of the saints.
They also surrounded the beloved city.
Fire came down from heaven.
The fire consumed the army.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀνέβησαν ἐπὶ τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐκύκλευσαν τὴν παρεμβολὴν τῶν ἁγίων καὶ τὴν πόλιν τὴν ἠγαπημένην καὶ κατέβη πῦρ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτούς

passages.text: And the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, into which the beast and the false prophet had already been thrown. There they will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
passages.sermon:
The devil is a deceiver.
The devil had deceived the nations.
God threw the devil into the lake of fire and sulfur.
The beast was already in the lake of fire and sulfur.
The false prophet was already in the lake of fire and sulfur.
The devil, the beast, and the false prophet will be tormented there.
They will be tormented day and night.
Their torment will last forever and ever.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ διάβολος ὁ πλανῶν αὐτοὺς ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου ὅπου καὶ τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων

passages.text: Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them.
passages.sermon:
John saw a great white throne.
God sat on the throne.
Earth and heaven saw God’s face.
Earth and heaven fled from God.
No place remained for earth and heaven.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδον θρόνον μέγαν λευκὸν καὶ τὸν καθήμενον ἐπ’ αὐτόν οὗ ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου ἔφυγεν ἡ γῆ καὶ ὁ οὐρανός καὶ τόπος οὐχ εὑρέθη αὐτοῖς

passages.text: And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And there were open books, and one of them was the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books.
passages.sermon:
John saw a vision from God.
He saw the dead people.
These dead people were both great and small.
They stood before the throne.
God sat on the throne.
Books were open before the throne.
One book was the Book of Life.
The dead were judged by God.
God judged them by what was written in the books.
The books recorded their deeds.
passages.original: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς νεκρούς τοὺς μεγάλους καὶ τοὺς μικρούς ἑστῶτας ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ βιβλία ἠνοίχθησαν Καὶ ἄλλο βιβλίον ἠνοίχθη ὅ ἐστιν τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἐκρίθησαν οἱ νεκροὶ ἐκ τῶν γεγραμμένων ἐν τοῖς βιβλίοις κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν

passages.text: The sea gave up its dead, and Death and Hades gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
passages.sermon:
God sat on a great white throne.
He judged all people.
The sea gave up the dead who were in it.
Death gave up the dead who were in it.
Hades gave up the dead who were in it.
Each person stood before God.
God judged each person by what they had done.
passages.original: καὶ ἔδωκεν ἡ θάλασσα τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἔδωκαν τοὺς νεκροὺς τοὺς ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκρίθησαν ἕκαστος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν

passages.text: Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
passages.sermon:
Death is a power that brings the end of life.
Hades is the place where the dead wait.
God threw Death into the lake of fire.
God threw Hades into the lake of fire.
The lake of fire is the second death.
The second death is final and complete.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ὁ ᾅδης ἐβλήθησαν εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός οὗτος ὁ θάνατος ὁ δεύτερός ἐστιν ἡ λίμνη τοῦ πυρός

passages.text: And if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire.
passages.sermon:
God keeps a Book of Life.
The Book of Life contains the names of those who belong to God.
God judges every person.
If God does not find a person's name in the Book of Life, He acts.
God throws that person into the lake of fire.
passages.original: καὶ εἴ τις οὐχ εὑρέθη ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ τῆς ζωῆς γεγραμμένος ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρός
